quotes.summary_phrase: Tyrese Maxey on his interest in studying sports psychology
quotes.excerpt: I need to figure out something to do with psychology once I'm done.

quotes.excerpt: Now you're almost like the people's therapist. It's a higher level and it's unique.
quotes.quote: When you're done, now you're almost like the people's therapist. It's a higher level and it's unique. There's nobody else trying to find that lane.

quotes.speaker: Tyrese Maxey
quotes.summary_phrase: Tyrese Maxey on why everyone needs a therapist
quotes.excerpt: I feel like everybody needs a therapist.
quotes.quote: I feel like everybody needs a therapist. I really do feel like everybody needs a therapist. There's a lot of things that people go through as a child that they don't unpack fully, and they don't have people to really talk to about that.

quotes.speaker: Tyrese Maxey
quotes.summary_phrase: Tyrese Maxey on his father's influence on his basketball career
quotes.excerpt: My dad was like, it's in the family, you play basketball, you got to quit.
quotes.quote: I played baseball first, and I love baseball. My dad was like, it's in the family, you play basketball, you got to quit. So I resented my dad for that for a while. And then when I got to my junior high school, something just clicked for me. That's why I started driving. I would drive myself to the gym. I would be there from 8:00 to 6:00 p.m. during the summertime, just there, always working and working.

quotes.speaker: Drew Hanlen
quotes.summary_phrase: Drew Hanlen on his early career financial struggles
quotes.excerpt: I got a check for $2 in the month of December in 1991.
quotes.quote: I got a check for $2 in the month of December in 1991. In that year, I made $1,240. And then they guaranteed me a $1,000 a month guaranteed salary if I would move to California from Missouri. And I was like, excuse me?
